subtitle: A mercenary career moves to Mars

body: Armored Core 2 is FromSoftware's PlayStation 2 mecha combat game, first released in Japan on 3 August 2000. Decades after the earlier trilogy, the colonisation of Mars has created another setting for corporate conflict and paid military work. The player assembles an Armored Core, takes contracts and confronts the Frighteners, a force threatening the established order. The move to new hardware gives the machines another level of detail, but the central relationship remains familiar. A battle tests decisions made in the garage, and its rewards make the next set of modifications possible.

Missions and Arena duels give a customised machine different tasks. A build that carries enough firepower for one contract may need another balance of speed or endurance against a rival pilot. The player learns how parts work together rather than treating each upgrade as an isolated improvement. Local multiplayer adds another test, allowing two players to confront one another with their own designs. The garage therefore supplies a continuing problem to solve: what should be changed after the last encounter, and which useful capability might be lost in making that adjustment?

Mechanical artist Shōji Kawamori returned, while a group including Tsukasa Saitoh and Kota Hoshino supplied the music. Armored Core 2 accompanied the PlayStation 2's North American launch in October 2000, with Europe following in January 2001. Another Age expanded this period of the series the following year. The game carries the original trilogy's workshop and mercenary structure onto a new machine without removing the need for deliberate preparation. Its attraction comes from seeing a personal design leave the garage and discovering whether the idea behind it survives contact with the battlefield.
